summary: Well-motivated, narrowly scoped preregistered experiment investigating retrieval- and tool-channel prompt-injection against an agentic NetOps prototype with a layered defense. The authors provide a rich, hashed artifact bundle and explicitly disclose integrity/caching issues that materially limit confirmatory inference. The reported confirmatory contrast (baseline vs combined defense) shows very high attack-success in both conditions and no significant reduction under the implemented combined defense; however, unresolved internal inconsistencies in counting and deterministic call-cache reuse undermine statistical independence, planned sampling, and the validity of the confirmatory claim.
critical_issues: Major deviation from preregistered sampling: planned paired runs (preregistered 160 paired units per confirmatory contrast) were not completed (complete_pairs=150) and planned total runs described in preregistration (640) were not executed; this reduces power and departs from the frozen design without documented, justified deviation handling.

Deterministic call-cache materially reduced external model calls (model_calls_used=163 for 300 completed episodes) and is documented in artifacts; cache reuse can induce dependence across runs/conditions and invalidates the independence assumption underlying the paired analysis unless explicitly demonstrated otherwise.

Internal integrity inconsistency: the artifact bundle contains conflicting marginal tallies vs paired contingency tables (the manuscript admits this). Without reprocessing or a reconciled recount, the reported paired counts and derived statistics cannot be relied upon.

Planned conditions/contrasts incompletely reported: preregistration specified four defense configurations (none, RAG-only, validator-only, combined) and two model families; the confirmatory results report only baseline vs combined-guarded and provide no confirmatory/ exploratory summaries for RAG-only or validator-only or model-family stratification as preregistered.

Missing per-run provenance mapping in manuscript: it is unclear from reported summary which model family/version produced each run and whether cached responses were reused across condition labels; per-run mapping (task id → condition → model id → cache-hash) must be shown for audit and to evaluate contamination.

Counting/exclusion transparency incomplete: although exclusion rules are stated, the manuscript does not provide a reconciled list of excluded run IDs, the exact parser-failure counts per run, or a deterministic reprocessing log to explain the observed inconsistency.

Statistical validity compromised: even if McNemar is appropriate for paired binary outcomes, cache-induced dependence and the unresolved counting inconsistency render the p-value and bootstrap CIs unreliable for the preregistered estimand.
required_revisions: Provide a deterministic, auditable reconciliation of the artifact counts: publish and explain a run-level table (task_id, model_family/version, condition, cache_file_hash, provider_call_id, parser_status, score, inclusion/exclusion reason) that reconciles marginal and paired tallies; re-run the frozen analysis pipeline on that reconciled table and republish corrected paired counts and statistics.

Demonstrate whether and how call_cache entries were reused across different condition labels. If cached responses were reused across baseline vs guarded labels, either (a) reprocess/recompute the confirmatory analysis excluding runs affected by cross-condition cache reuse, or (b) rerun the affected runs without cache reuse according to the preregistered stopping/retry rules.

If rerun is infeasible, produce a sensitivity analysis that quantifies the effect of cache reuse on the primary estimand (worst-case/best-case imputation and recalculated paired-test results) and transparently update the manuscript conclusions accordingly.

Publish per-condition, per-model-family breakdowns (including RAG-only and validator-only) as preregistered (or document and justify why those planned contrasts were not performed), with corresponding inclusion/exclusion counts and CI/p-value treatment per the multiplicity plan.

Document all deviations from the preregistration explicitly in a deviations table (what changed, why, when) and update the power analysis given the realized sample size; if power is inadequate for the primary estimand, label the result exploratory and avoid confirmatory claims.
Resolve and document parser-determinism issues: publish parser failure examples, formal parser acceptance criteria, and rerun or re-evaluate affected outputs so that exclusion rules are reproducible.
optional_revisions: Increase model/version coverage and report per-model-family susceptibility to improve external validity (if resources permit).
Rerun a subset of preregistered pairs without deterministic call_cache to validate independence and to estimate cache bias directly.
Provide worked examples of specific successful adversarial payloads and example guarded pipeline traces illustrating why the defense failed for those cases, to support mechanistic understanding.
Include an explicit analysis showing RAG-only and validator-only marginal contributions to attack reduction (exploratory analyses), as originally planned.
Add short scripting/notebook instructions enabling an independent auditor to re-run the deterministic reprocessing and reproduce the reconciled paired table from the raw artifacts.
